title: Cisco IOS XE web UI privilege escalation (creates admin account)
remediation: Upgrade to a fixed release (17.9.4a, 17.6.6a, 17.3.8a, 16.12.10a or later). Until then run 'no ip http server' and 'no ip http secure-server', and check for unknown local accounts.

title: Cisco IOS XE web UI command injection (root implant)
remediation: Upgrade to a fixed release. Until then disable the HTTP/HTTPS server.

title: Plain HTTP management server enabled
remediation: Run 'no ip http server'. If the web UI is needed, use 'ip http secure-server' restricted by an ACL.

title: ISR4331/K9 is end of sale; support is ending
remediation: Add the device to the hardware refresh plan.

title: Default SNMP community string
remediation: Remove the default community and move to SNMPv3 (authPriv).

title: SNMP read-write community configured
remediation: Remove RW communities; use SNMPv3 with read-only views for monitoring.

title: 'enable password' used instead of 'enable secret'
remediation: Replace with 'enable secret' (type 8 or 9) and remove 'enable password'.

title: 2811 is past vendor end of support
remediation: Plan a hardware replacement. Until then, restrict management access to a dedicated management network.

title: Telnet allowed on VTY lines
remediation: Under 'line vty 0 15' set 'transport input ssh'.

title: Password encryption service disabled
remediation: Run 'service password-encryption' (and prefer type 8/9 secrets).

title: No remote syslog server
remediation: Configure 'logging host <syslog-server>'.

title: No NTP server configured
remediation: Configure 'ntp server <server>' so log timestamps are reliable.

title: No login banner
remediation: Add a 'banner login' with an authorised-use warning.

title: PHP2Shell: PHP memory corruption on out-of-memory handling (remote code execution)
remediation: Upgrade PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 or later (Linux distribution packages: install the vendor's security update). Interim only (partial): set session.upload_progress.enabled=0, block multipart/form-data requests at the WAF where uploads aren't needed, or put the application behind network-level authentication.
